If you prefer a one-pager PDF for procurement, say the word and I’ll export.

Quick answers (summary):
1) TAM coverage model:
   - Named TAM for account (Primary TAM: Marissa Cole) — business-hours coverage (M-F 8am-6pm PT) for proactive account work and weekly syncs.
   - 24/7 operational on-call for Sev 1 incidents via Support rotation (see below). TAM engages automatically for Sev 1 and is on-call for major incident coordination when active.
2) Escalation path (Sev 1 / Sev 2):
   - Initial response (support tier): 
     - Sev 1: ack within 15 minutes; engineer engaged within 30 minutes.
     - Sev 2: ack within 1 hour; engineer engaged within 4 hours.
   - If initial engineer cannot remediate within SLA window, escalates to on-call senior engineer and then to SRE leads. TAM and CS Director are notified at escalation step.
3) On-call rotation length and roles:
   - Support on-call rotation: 1 week per engineer, 4-person rotation typical for a region.
   - Primary/backup: each week has a primary on-call and an adjacent backup; the TAM is not the primary on-call but is notified for Sev 1 and acts as customer liaison.
4) Incident communication cadence:
   - Initial ack: within 15 minutes for Sev 1, within 1 hour for Sev 2.
   - Updates: every 30 minutes during active Sev 1 until stable; every 2-4 hours for Sev 2 depending on impact.
   - Postmortem: internal postmortem within 72 hours; customer-facing RCA within 5 business days (unless legal/regulatory timing requires acceleration).
5) Carve-outs for Dedicated/Private:
   - Dedicated: same SLAs for support response; longer resolution expectations if customer-managed network or on-prem hardware is implicated (we specify responsible party in mutual action plan).
   - Private (air-gapped/on-prem): support engagement requires remote access agreements; we provide runbooks and assisted runbook sessions; on-site support available as a billable add-on.

Attachments: StorBank_Support_Observability_Matrix.xlsx (matrix workbook), TAM_Roster_v2.pdf (named TAMs + escalation contacts).

Best,
